newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 5 to 913 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 5 to 913 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 913 as of April 11, down five from the prior week and 178 above the year-ago total of 735, Baker Hughes Inc. reported.
The number of rigs drilling on land fell by three to 760, while rigs working offshore dipped by one to 126.

The number of rigs active in inland waters dipped by one to 27. Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Michigan and Oklahamo, which were both down by eight, and Texas, which was up by six.
Gulf of Mexico fell by one to 121.

A total of 371 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down 13 from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas was up by eight to 541, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained at one.
In Canada, the number of working rigs was down 41 at 204 vs. 84 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.
There were 166 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of April 11, down one from the period ending April 4, Offshore Data Services said Friday.
The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 179, was 92.7 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area remained unchanged at 103 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 104, a utilization rate of 99.0 percent.
The worldwide rig count was up one at 573 out of a total fleet of 604, making the utilization rate 94.9 percent.
